hero: The Storymaker’s Video Channel Book cover

problem.h: They want a channel. You’d rather they waited.
p: Lots of children dream of having their own video channel, with a name, a logo and a show of their own.
They aren’t ready for a camera, an account or the internet watching, but the ideas are already bursting out.

approach.h: The whole channel, all on paper
p: The book lets them dream up, design and plan six video channels without a camera, a phone or an account. Every page is for drawing and writing.
Each channel has fifteen pages, from the channel file and logo to storyboards, scripts and a premiere night poster.

offer.p: Big A4 pages with room for every storyboard and thumbnail.
features: Logos, banners, hosts, storyboards and scripts, fifteen pages per channel.
Ten quick lessons, from channel ideas and thumbnails to filming tips and being kind online.
A safety promise to sign with a grown-up, and no camera, phone or account needed.

proof.p: More pages from inside coming soon.
note: I made this for the children who are always telling me about the channel they’re going to have one day. This way they can have six, on paper, with no camera needed.
I love the premiere night poster. Seeing their show “go live” on the page makes it feel real.

items: Ten Creator’s Academy lessons: channel ideas, names and logos, banners, scripts, storyboards, thumbnails and being kind online
A host or mascot for every channel

100 video ideas for when inspiration runs dry
A Creator ID card and a safety promise to sign with a grown-up
A Creator of the Year certificate
112 pages in total, A4, on white paper

points: One paperback book, printed and posted by Amazon.
No subscription and nothing to download. Open it and start.
Amazon handles delivery and returns, just like anything else you buy there.

faq: Roughly seven to twelve. Younger children love the logos and mascots, and older ones will enjoy writing scripts and planning episodes.
Do they need a camera, phone or account?
No. Everything happens on paper with a pencil. Nothing goes online.
Do they need to be good at drawing?
No. Storyboard and thumbnail frames give them a start, and stick figures are fine for everything else.
How is it different from The Storymaker’s Comic Book?
The Comic Book is for telling stories in panels. This one is about planning whole channels, from the logo to the premiere night.
